answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a market, with voting weight capped per bond and slashed when a fraud challenge proves coordinated deception. One operator can still create many identities, but each must lock real capital, and splitting the bond does not multiply influence. The rule works whether an agent trades tundra sensors, tracks a zenith launch, or maps karst caves; the attacker pays in tied-up funds and forfeited bonds, not merely the trivial cost of minting accounts.
